items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: And I know I mentioned that the singer there was Chippy Hill. She was a blues singer.

ctx.x: He had a band. Okay, it was Errol Garner, myself and Slam. Slam Stewart Trio. Howard McGhee's band and Coleman Hawkins, it was his first time in Europe since the war, you know. He left because of the war, and this was his first trip, which was like a triumphal return, you know. And I know I mentioned that the singer there was Chippy Hill. She was a blues singer. Yeah. But the one thing that I remembered about that trip was how fanatical the French people were about jazz. Traditional jazz as opposed to bop.

Now, as you know Howard McGhee was a bebop. This is the bebop era. Of course our group spanned both eras, and so did Coleman Hawkins, but the main bone of contention was Howard McGhee's group, and we played at the Marini Theatre, it's right at the foot of the Champs Elysees. And Panassie had bought a block of seats and they came there to boo, and they would boo, you know. They actually came -- every concert they were there and they would whistle, boo, you know, because
